title: Photorealistic avatar uncanny valley
bottleneck: Avatars that are almost-but-not-quite human trigger revulsion: codec avatars need heavy capture rigs and per-person training, real-time facial tracking misses microexpressions, and rendering skin, eyes, and hair convincingly at 90fps is brutally expensive. Stylized avatars dodge the valley but sacrifice presence for professional use.
why_it_blocks: Believable faces are the key to VR communication replacing video calls; the uncanny valley keeps avatars in the realm of cartoons. Telepresence can't go mainstream looking wrong.
current_state: Research codec avatars are stunning in demos with dedicated capture; consumer headsets offer decent but clearly synthetic avatars. Real-time photorealism for everyone is unsolved. Microexpressions and eye moisture are extraordinarily hard to render in real time, and their absence reads immediately as lifelessness. Capturing a personal codec avatar still needs a specialized rig, so most users get generic faces instead.
